headline: Approved accepting a restricted gift for replacing the library's wooden fence and a staff holiday gift from investment funds.
summary: Miss Mansfield reported a record 13,542 visitors in October and a one-day bathroom shutdown after plumbing backed up. The fountain was shut down, with $2,600 left in its account, and heating system repairs are still ongoing. Trustees asked staff to contact a local artist about a painting he offered to donate.

plain_text:
Draft of Minutes of Board of Trustees Meeting of November 19, 2026 
Salem, Massachusetts        November 19, 2026 
A meeting of the Board of Trustees was held via Zoom on this date at 4:06pm with Trustees 
April, Austin, Lutts, Morin, Rourke, and Trustee Buckley present and presiding. Mayor Pangallo 
was absent. Miss Mansfield was present. 
Approval of draft minutes from September 17, 2026 UNANIMOUS. 
Current Library Use reports were distributed. Salem was fourth highest in NOBLE for 
circulation of physical items during September and fifth highest in October. Salem was second 
highest in Overdrive/Libby circulation during September and October. Miss Mansfield reported 
that the library had a record-breaking 13,542 visitors in October, and noted that the library was 
closed for both Indigenous Peoples’ Day and on Halloween. Miss Mansfield reported that tourist 
bathroom use was overwhelming this year, and that the bathrooms had to be shut down one 
Saturday due to the plumbing in the building backing up. Miss Mansfield asked Destination 
Salem and Haunted Happenings to remove the library from the restroom locator information. 
Financial reports were distributed. Miss Mansfield reported that the executor of Dolores Jordan’s 
estate was in touch and she had left the library $20,000. Ms. Jordan was appreciative of the work 
the library does supporting immigrants. The Trustees expressed gratitude for the gift. 
A restricted gift agreement was presented to the Trustees for the purposes of replacing the 
wooden fence. A motion to approve the agreement and accept the gift was made by Trustee 
Morin. Seconded by Trustee Lutts. UNANIMOUS 
 Trustee Lutts reported that he had reached out to the Salem Garden Club about the library’s 
landscaping needs. The Board meets on Tuesday and would discuss the idea and get back to 
Trustee Lutts next week. 
The traditional holiday gift for the library staff was discussed. Trustee April made a motion to 
continue the tradition and transfer the funds from the investments. Seconded by Trustee Rourke. 
UNANIMOUS 
Miss Mansfield reported that the library was still struggling to repair the heating system. The 
library recently switched to a new on call HVAC vendor and Miss Mansfield planned to have a 
half-day consultation with the controls system vendor. Miss Mansfield noted that capital funds 
were set aside for repairing the HVAC system this year. 
Miss Mansfield reported that Geoff Sampson from Aquatic Art had shut down the fountain and 
made some recommendations. He said that a consumable that costs $500 would be required in 
the spring, and noted that the uneven flow on the middle level of the fountain was due to water 
pooling and not draining properly. He recommended that holes be drilled in that level and that
rust resistant paint be used. Trustee Buckley asked about the balance of the fountain account, and 
Miss Mansfield reported there was currently $2,600 remaining. The invoice from Aquatic Art 
had not yet been issued. 
Miss Mansfield reported that a local artist named Jess Hermann had offered to donate a painting 
to the library. The Trustees admired the photo and discussed how the beautiful artwork could be 
used for fundraising. The Trustees asked Miss Mansfield to reach out to the artist to ask if the 
gift included the exclusive rights, title, and interests of the piece. Trustee Morin noted he would 
be happy to do a photo op with the artist. 
Trustee Buckley asked about the status of the memorial webpage for Miss Little. Miss Mansfield 
reported that it was not ready yet, but would be soon. 
Trustee Buckley noted that she would like the Trustees to develop a Gift Acceptance Policy. 
Trustees Rourke and April agreed that this was an excellent idea. Trustee Buckley noted that 
they could begin to work on it in the spring. 
Adjourned 4:38pm.
